paper_title: ChARM Character-based Act-adaptive Reward Modeling for Advanced   Role-Playing Language Agents
caption: The character distribution in RoleplayPref consists of 3 primary categories and 13 subcategories.

model_annotations.Bulgarian: This diagram presents the character distribution in RoleplayPref, structured as a sunburst (multi-level pie) chart with 3 primary categories in an inner ring and 13 subcategories in an outer ring. The innermost level shows three main categories: "Virtual Characters" in blue, occupying the largest portion of approximately 60-65% of the chart; "Custom Characters" in pink/green, taking up roughly 15-20%; and "Real Characters" in green, comprising approximately 15-20%. The outer ring further subdivides these categories: Virtual Characters breaks down into "Comic Characters," "Movie Characters," "Teleplay Characters," "Novel Characters," and "Game Characters," all shown in light blue shades, with Comic Characters and Novel Characters appearing to be among the larger subcategories. Custom Characters appears as a single pink segment in the outer ring. Real Characters subdivides into "Scientists," "Artists," "Athletes," "Writers," "Musicians," "Actors," and "Influencers," displayed in light green/peach tones, with each of these subcategories occupying relatively small and roughly comparable portions. The chart does not include a separate legend, but labels are placed directly on or near each segment. The segments within the Virtual Characters category collectively dominate the chart visually, while the Real Characters subcategories are arranged in a sequence from Scientists at the top to Influencers at the bottom of that section.
model_annotations.English: This chart is a sunburst (nested pie/donut) chart illustrating the character distribution in RoleplayPref, which consists of 3 primary categories and 13 subcategories. The inner ring displays three main categories: Virtual Characters (shown in blue, occupying the largest portion, roughly 55-60%), Custom Characters (shown in pink/green, approximately 15-20%), and Real Characters (shown in green, approximately 20-25%). The outer ring breaks these primary categories into subcategories. Under Virtual Characters (light blue outer segments), the subcategories include Comic Characters, Movie Characters, Teleplay Characters, Novel Characters, and Game Characters, with Comic Characters and Novel Characters appearing to be among the larger segments. Under Custom Characters (light pink outer segment), no further labeled subdivisions are visible beyond the single segment. Under Real Characters (light green outer segments), the subcategories include Scientists, Artists, Athletes, Writers, Musicians, Actors, and Influencers, each appearing as relatively thin slices suggesting smaller individual proportions. Labels are placed directly on or adjacent to each slice, and no separate legend is present. No explicit percentage values are displayed. The segments in the outer ring under Real Characters appear to be roughly similar in size to each other, while those under Virtual Characters vary more noticeably in size.
